messages:
anna_dev: Quick heads-up — seeing unexpected all-reduce tail on 8-GPU runs when KV prefetch is enabled. Nsight timeline shows long gaps between compute islands.

anna_dev: Capture command I used: `nsys profile -t cuda,cudnn,nvtx -o run1 ./serve --tp 2 --pp 4 --kv-prefetch`

anna_dev: Perf summary so far: baseline (no prefetch) tokens/sec ~6000; with prefetch drops to ~4200. All-reduce time per step jumps 1.1ms -> 4.6ms, but compute kernel durations look unchanged. :thinking:

mike_infra: do you have the nvtx ranges or waterfall screenshot? can you paste the TL link?

anna_dev: link: http://internal.s3/redwood/nsi/1769998765/waterfall.png

jeff_runtime: interesting — could be stream contention or a kernel selection side-effect. prefetch might be choosing a different matmul kernel (workspace/align) that hurts NCCL overlap.

lisa_ml: also check if KV prefetch does a reorder/copy on the same stream as NCCL. memcpy + kernel scheduling can block the comm stream.

anna_dev: nvprof snippet shows memcpy H2D around step boundary overlapping the all-reduce window. excerpt:
```
CUDA memcpy HtoD    0.45ms   0.47ms   [stream 1]
NCCL AllReduce     4.6ms    4.6ms    [stream 1]
```

perf-bot: Nsight capture ready: s3://perf-captures/1769998765.nsight (job 98765) :white_check_mark:

mike_infra: can you rerun with `--nvtx-kv` to explicitly mark KV ops and `--force-kernel=optimized` to force the alt matmul kernel? want to see if kernel selection changes timeline.

anna_dev: launching now with NVTX tags + forced kernel, will post results in ~10m

jeff_runtime: while that's running, add a tiny timer inside the allreduce wrapper to record GPU timestamps (cudaEventRecord) so we can disambiguate host scheduling vs GPU blocking. sample snippet:
```
cudaEventRecord(e1, comm_stream);
ncclAllReduce(..., comm_stream);
cudaEventRecord(e2, comm_stream);
cudaEventSynchronize(e2);
float ms; cudaEventElapsedTime(&ms, e1, e2);
```

lisa_ml: strongly suspect stream affinity. if KV copy uses default stream it may serialize work. try `cudaMemcpyAsync(..., kv_stream)` or `cudaStreamCreateWithFlags(&kv_stream, cudaStreamNonBlocking)`.

anna_dev: quick update: forced KV to separate non-blocking stream — tokens/sec recovered to ~5900, all-reduce back to ~1.2ms. Looks like stream contention + kernel choice together amplified the tail.

mike_infra: nice repro. can you add a small regression test that toggles kv_stream behavior and measures allreduce ms? put it in perf/unit/parallel_efficiency/*

anna_dev: filing ticket INF-2319 with repro, nvprof/nsight captures, and the small script: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/INF-2319

perf-bot: Regression test INF-2319 added to perf-runner queue :rocket:

lisa_ml: follow-up: after the fix, capture another nsight trace with NVTX tags for KV/AllReduce/Compute and attach to the ticket. good to have before/after waterfalls.

anna_dev: will attach after the next run. thanks everyone! :tada:
